D.treatment: distance-learning, e-learning, m-learning or web-based ultrasonography teaching

O.outcome_detail: overall ultrasonography learning and training quality

cells.quote: From analysis of these data, it was observed that teaching of ultrasonography using telemedicine methods is similar to the traditional method, except for venous access procedures, for which the studies did not show agreement.
cells.note: Systematic review synthesis; the included studies varied in outcomes and methods, and no meta-analysis was performed because of outcome variability.

O.outcome_detail: practical ultrasonography skills and ultrasound-guided procedures

cells.quote: From analysis of these data, it was observed that teaching of ultrasonography using telemedicine methods is similar to the traditional method, except for venous access procedures, for which the studies did not show agreement.
cells.note: The review reports similar practical performance overall, but disagreement or poorer performance for some venous-access procedures; some distance groups performed better on selected practical measures.

O.outcome_detail: retention of ultrasonography information after two weeks to two months

cells.quote: It was concluded that teaching via telemedicine provided results that were similar to those through the traditional methodology, including in a questionnaire administered four weeks after the teaching, to evaluate the retention of information.
cells.note: The text reports similarity but does not report an equivalence test or adequate power for the pooled retention finding, so the direction is coded ns.

cells.quote: We found that learning via telemedicine methodologies presents great acceptance among students, besides demonstrating quality similar to the traditional method.
cells.note: The study text reports acceptance but does not provide a direct comparative effect or statistical result for this outcome.

cells.note: Systematic review synthesis; no pooled effect size was computed.

O.outcome_detail: self-reported frequency of supervisor assistance during IJV cannulation

cells.quote: The proportion reporting frequent supervisor assistance (often or sometimes) was lower with ultrasound-guided than with landmark-based cannulation for both IJV (40.22% vs. 63.96%) and RA (36.26% vs. 63.30%) access (all P < 0.001; Fig. 3).
cells.note: Ultrasound-guided cannulation was associated with less frequent assistance; the paired comparison used McNemar’s test.

O.outcome_detail: First-attempt success for internal jugular vein cannulation

cells.quote: The ultrasound-guided technique was associated with a higher proportion of first-attempt cannulation for both IJV (71.37% vs. 36.34%) and RA (64.76% vs. 30.40%) (both P < 0.001).
cells.note: Self-reported survey comparison; the cross-sectional design does not establish causation.
